identity: A physics multiple-choice bank (electricity, momentum, stellar end-states, thermometers): 20 questions, one per printed line, each with a stem and FOUR options. The file carries heavy OCR damage - the lam-alif ligature has broken so al-ammeter appears as al-ameter with a doubled alif (األميتر، االوميتر، قليال، وصالت، ال تتغير، ألعلى، ألسفل), and nisbiyyan is split into two tokens (نسبي ا).
law: MCQ BANK (section I), unchanged. Median line 21, but a line is a question: I2 the stem is ONE unit ending where the four siblings start, I3 each option is its own unit, I5 an internal wa never cuts. 459 real tokens / 100 units = 4.6 per unit, exactly the biology-bank figure.
reasoning: The constant FOUR is the check, and it resolved every ambiguous line. Five lines end the stem on a dangling function word: @42, @80, @102 on huwa, @262 on hiya, @116 and @183 on bi-sabab. @354 ends on the copula yakun with the four predicates following, and @405 ends on yusawi. The hardest line was @48-@62, where the four options are unit expressions whose slashes and dots were stripped: kulum th | kulum th | nyutn kulum | nyutn kulum - two pairs that are identical as bare tokens because the original distinguished coulomb/second from coulomb.second. I resolved it by counting: 8 tokens after the stem, four options, therefore 2 tokens each. The same reasoning fixed @327-@345, where option 1 is four tokens (tesla m th kulum) and options 2-4 are three each, and where options 2 and 4 are again identical strings. @378-@405 is the longest stem in the document (28 tokens, with an internal fa-wasalat and wa-irtaddat) and 0h forbids cutting inside it - the four options are the four signed impulse values, and had I fired the coordinator rule on the stems fa- and wa- I would have produced six or seven units on that line. Broken tokens are kept with their option: nisbi + a is one word split by OCR and I did NOT put a boundary between them, on either @437 or @457; la yatafaal and la tujad keep their negative particle. 0s is satisfied - all twenty lines are stem plus four.
